# open-security-summit.sgit.ai: the next Open Security Summit website

> The Open Security Summit: working sessions where every participant is a presenter,
> in person from 2017 to 2019, online from 2020, restarting in 2026 with a regular run of short working
> sessions called when the participants can make them, events in London, and a programme of hosted open projects. This site is where the next
> version of open-security-summit.org is built in the open.

Site version: v0.1.2. Run by Open Security Summit CIC (UK, company 11935098).
Content CC BY 4.0, code Apache 2.0. Source: https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Open-Security-Summit

## The honest sentence

WHAT RUNS: these pages, the summit history, a first archive of notable sessions linking to
open-security-summit.org, the hosted-projects proposal, the first session page (php2shell), the first sponsors (RiskMandate, The
Cyber Boardroom, SGit.ai, all connected to the CIC's director). PLANNED, NOT RUNNING: participant
pages, the full archive as data, session follow-ups, personalised paths, registration. NO
DATES are set for the php2shell session, later sessions or the London events. Agent Behaviour Policies as the first
hosted project is a PROPOSAL, for discussion and legal review. /about/#status is the authority.

## Pages

- [About this site](https://open-security-summit.sgit.ai/about/): What open-security-summit.sgit.ai is, how it relates to open-security-summit.org, what runs today and what does not, and the rules this site keeps so it does not drift into the technical debt that stalled the last one.
- [Archive](https://open-security-summit.sgit.ai/archive/): A first selection from the Open Security Summit's archive, 2018 to 2024: keynotes, working sessions and recordings, with links to the session pages and videos.
- [Articles](https://open-security-summit.sgit.ai/articles/): Articles about the Open Security Summit: its history, why it stalled, and what it is doing next.
- [Events](https://open-security-summit.sgit.ai/events/): The Open Security Summit restarts with a regular run of short working sessions, called when the participants can make them, starting with php2shell; then in-person events in London. What is planned and how to take part.
- [Fund the summit](https://open-security-summit.sgit.ai/fund/): Why the Open Security Summit needs funding now, what the money pays for, and the rule that sponsorship buys no content.
- [History](https://open-security-summit.sgit.ai/history/): The history of the Open Security Summit and the OWASP summits before it: 2008 and 2011 in Portugal, three in-person weeks at Woburn Forest from 2017 to 2019, online from 2020, the pause in 2025, and the restart in 2026.
- [Open Security Summit](https://open-security-summit.sgit.ai/): The Open Security Summit: working sessions where developers and security people work together and every participant is a presenter. Restarting in 2026 with events in London, remote sessions, and a home for open security projects.
- [Participate](https://open-security-summit.sgit.ai/participate/): How the Open Security Summit works: working sessions, not talks; every participant is a presenter; outcomes written down; and, new in this version, a page and a follow-up for every participant.
- [Hosted projects](https://open-security-summit.sgit.ai/projects/): The Open Security Summit CIC proposes to host open projects that need an independent home, starting with Agent Behaviour Policies. What hosting means, what it does not, and how a project can apply.
- [Session: php2shell](https://open-security-summit.sgit.ai/sessions/php2shell/): The first of the Open Security Summit's new working sessions: php2shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), the disclosure that broke, AI-assisted discovery, the agencies' offline advice, and the unsupported PHP versions. How to take part.
- [The next phase: Open Security Summit sessions called when the participants can make them, not a week-long event, starting with the php2shell PHP flaws](https://open-security-summit.sgit.ai/articles/the-next-phase-ad-hoc-sessions.html): The next phase of the Open Security Summit is not a big week-long event. It is a regular run of short working sessions, each called when the people who need to be in it can make it, on subjects that matter now, each with a page, an outcome and a follow-up. The aim is to start generating energy and sponsors again, and the bigger London events come out of that. The first session will be on php2shell, the two critical PHP flaws of October 2026, which the SGit newsroom is covering as evidence.
- [When the website stalled the summit: what technical debt did to the Open Security Summit, and why now is the time to restart it](https://open-security-summit.sgit.ai/articles/when-the-website-stalled-the-summit.html): The Open Security Summit has some of the best material in application security, and it stalled. Not for lack of ideas or people, but because its website drifted into complexity and technical debt that nobody had the time to refactor, and because there was never the capacity to follow up. The numbers from its repositories, what was lost, and why, with agents now able to do the follow-up, it is time to restart it, in London and online.
